描述_ZN: Confucius Temple Monument", written and written by Yu Shinan in the Tang Dynasty, with the forehead written by Li Dan, the king of the Sangha. It was erected in the seventh year of Emperor Taizong's reign (633). The inscription is in regular script, with 35 lines and 64 characters. The height of the tablet is 400 cm and the width is 150 cm. The inscription records the establishment of Kong Delun, the 33rd grandson of Confucius, as the Marquis of Praise and the restoration of the Temple of Confucius in the 9th year of Wu De (626). According to legend, only a few dozen copies of this inscription were made and given to the ministers during the Zhenguan period, but the stone was destroyed by fire. In the third year of Wu Zhou Chang'an (703), Empress Wu ordered King Li Dan to re-carve and write the tablet, which was later destroyed by fire. There are two existing re-carvings: one is the early Song Dynasty Wang Yanchao re-carving, the monument in Xi'an, Shaanxi Province, commonly known as "Shaanxi Ben", "Shaanxi Ben" or "West Temple Hall"; one is said to be the Yuan Dynasty re-carving, the monument in Shandong It is said to have been re-carved during the Yuan and Yuan dynasties, and is located in Chengwu County, Shandong Province, commonly known as "Chengwu Ben" or "East Temple Hall". The former word is fatter, and the latter word is thinner.　　The topography is a white paper with a border cut and framed in white paper. A total of 17 and a half openings, each half opening 28.5 cm long, 16.3 cm across. At the end of the line, "The emperor's virtue and the Confucian breeze Yongxuan Jinshi" has not been danced. Inscribed with the signature of Jue'an, six paragraphs of postscript by Bao Shichen, Sun Xingyan, Song Baocun and Chen Qijun, and six paragraphs of observational markings by Yao Nai, Zhao Huaiyu, Wu Rongguang and Zhang Weiping, The Seal of the Temple Hall of Confucius" is inscribed with 31 seals, including "Kuan", "Ji Mu Fu", "Bao's Secret Play", "Shichen Xue Gu", and "Huaiyu Private Seal".　　The calligraphic style of the Confucius Temple Monument is handsome and rounded, with slightly longer and more beautiful characters, flat across and straight down, and with an expansive stroke. The calligraphy of this stele has been valued by calligraphers of the Jin Shi dynasty, who called it a masterpiece of the regular script of the Tang Dynasty, the ultimate rule of regular script. In the early Ming Dynasty, Zhang Shen commented on the stele: "The calligraphy and painting are unique to Zhong and Wang, and no one has been able to match them in thousands of years."　　It was recorded in the books of Song Ouyang Xiu's "The End of Jigu Lu" and Zhao Mingcheng's "Jin Shi Lu", and in the books of Qing Sun Chengze's "Geng Zi Pin Xia Ji" and Gu Yanwu's "Jin Shi Wen Ji".
